hypothesis: Reducing validated NN-vine simulator exposure from 1000 to 100 unique episode presentations improves transfer to historical fine-tuning, evaluated separately for the original full observation and the focused-analysis preferred no-policy-visible-dependence observation.
design_revision_reason: The completed two-window retrospective analysis found that the no-policy-visible-dependence ensemble ranked first by CRRA certainty equivalent in both windows, whereas the scenario-CVaR-only observation did not improve on it. The unlaunched dose experiment was therefore revised before freezing or training.
selection_disclosure: The no-policy-visible-dependence architecture was selected after viewing retrospective w01/w02 results. All dose-response results remain post-holdout explanatory and cannot provide confirmatory model selection evidence.

experiments.scientific_question: Does lower simulator exposure improve the original full-state TD3-LSTM policy?

Does lower simulator exposure improve the focused-analysis preferred TD3-LSTM policy when raw vine features and scenario-CVaR are both hidden from the policy while dependence-informed pretraining and reward remain active?

decision_rule: A favorable same-holdout result is hypothesis-generating only. The completed focused windows select the no-policy-visible architecture but do not validate the 100-path dose; dose support requires a future dose-specific walk-forward, independent external market, or genuinely new observations.
